exactly_three_classes.name: Personal-use projects
exactly_three_classes.purpose: Solve an actual problem, need or friction in the learner's own life, study, sport, creative workflow, household role or personal system.
exactly_three_classes.success_test: The learner's original problem is measurably or demonstrably better addressed; the learner can explain the change and its limits.
must_have: A real learner-owned problem observed or stated before solution design
A defined user (normally the learner) and context
A practical artefact, process or demonstrated change
A review of whether the solution actually helps
must_not_require: A polished product or commercial viability
valid_stop_conditions: Problem turns out to be unimportant
Trial causes extra burden or risk
A smaller non-digital change solves it better

exactly_three_classes.name: Product/business-foundation projects
exactly_three_classes.purpose: Build something useful with a credible path to later improvement, packaging, distribution and potential sale, while testing assumptions before committing resources.
exactly_three_classes.success_test: A bounded product/service prototype or operational foundation is tested against a real task, with evidence about problem fit, quality, delivery, cost, capacity, risk and next decision.
must_have: A useful artefact or service prototype
Testable acceptance criteria and failure cases
Basic operational and unit-economics reasoning appropriate to scope
Privacy, safety, legal/platform and ethical boundaries
must_not_require: Claims of product-market fit from small samples
valid_stop_conditions: Risk or legal/platform conditions are unsuitable
Prototype fails the core user task
A different approach is more proportionate

exactly_three_classes.name: Intrinsic/for-its-own-sake projects
exactly_three_classes.purpose: Explore, investigate, make, play, compose, collect, experiment or create because the subject itself is interesting or meaningful to the learner.
exactly_three_classes.success_test: The learner has genuinely explored a chosen question or creative direction and can describe observations, choices, discoveries, uncertainty or new curiosity.
must_have: A learner-chosen curiosity, fascination, expressive intention or puzzle
Some trace of exploration, iteration or observation
A reflection on what was discovered or what remains open
valid_stop_conditions: The exploration reveals a better question
The learner chooses to pause or abandon it

separation_rules: Do not classify by subject matter alone; classify by the project's primary reason for existing and its success condition.
A digital app can be personal-use if it solves the learner's own problem; product/business-foundation only if it is designed and tested as a useful offer for a defined user beyond the learner.
A research project can be intrinsic exploration if driven by curiosity; personal-use if it informs an actual personal decision; product/business-foundation if it tests a product/service opportunity.
An art project remains intrinsic when no client or utility is required, even if the finished work could later be sold.
Projects may produce transferable skills, but transfer is evidence to capture, not a requirement imposed on intrinsic projects.
Teamwork, research, design, software, writing and public presentation are methods or formats, not additional project classes.
Never merge the three classes into one generic project template. Shared metadata may exist, but purpose, success criteria, risk model and assessment emphasis remain class-specific.
selection_algorithm: Ask why the learner wants to do this project.
Identify the primary beneficiary and success condition.
If the primary beneficiary is the learner and success means improving their own real context, choose personal_use.
If the purpose is to build a useful offer/system for a defined user and test its future delivery/commercial path, choose product_business_foundation.
If the purpose is curiosity, expression, experimentation or creation without a utility requirement, choose intrinsic_exploration.
If more than one purpose is genuinely present, split into separate linked projects or choose one primary class and record secondary motivations; do not blend class criteria.
